leverage.exposure: No leverage, now or after the bid resolves. The balance is positive today and stays positive if the bid lands, and it is the only live offer in the portfolio, so there is no scenario this cycle in which two bids clear at once and push the balance negative. That matters because a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday, which outranks every other consideration. The headline spending power figure is a trap this close to a lock, since it is measured against the floor rather than against cash; the real ceiling until the matchday locks is cash on hand, and after the committed bid that leaves only a small amount uncommitted. The unwind ceiling is equally tight: at eleven players no sale is legal at all, and one buy permits exactly one sale.

binding_gap: The binding gap is a fourth outfield body, and specifically a midfielder, because at eleven players there is no bench and a blank in the starting side cannot be substituted out. Filling it is what the Onyeka bid does, and it is also what unlocks the only legal sale. Until a twelfth player lands, the squad is simultaneously legal and completely rigid, which is why fixing this gap outranks every possible upgrade to a slot Georg can already fill.

sell.reason: Amoako remains the designated first funding sale, and it stays strictly conditional on the Onyeka buy landing first. Ligainsider's profile, checked this run, marks him fit but records no starts and no substitute appearances in this season's Bundesliga, only bench inclusions, and HSV's probable eleven for the Mainz trip on 6 September, page updated 1 September, does not list him. He is also the only points-free sale on the books: the best eleven after the Onyeka buy simply drops him, so the sale banks cash without costing a single fielded point, whereas selling Widmer or Bernardo instead would force Amoako's blank back into the side. Lokonga, Widmer and Bernardo are all holds and all three sit in the best eleven. Lokonga is confirmed in HSV's probable midfield; the value complaint against him on points per euro is still true but he is load-bearing at this squad size.

standing.name: Amoako
standing.why: STRICTLY CONDITIONAL ON THE ONYEKA BUY (Bqf56ma) LANDING FIRST. At eleven players NO sale is legal - selling anyone drops the squad to TEN, which cannot field an eleven and takes the -100 PENALTY. THIS CHANGES THE FUNDING-SALE ORDER AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Earlier runs designated Widmer, Bernardo and Lokonga as the funding sales. Those are all WRONG as the first sale once Onyeka lands, because all three sit in the best eleven while Amoako does not. Worked from the ap: with Onyeka the squad is 12 = 1GK/5DEF/4MID/2ATT and the best shape is 5-3-2 dropping Amoako, fielded ap 1395 (GK 129 + DEF 138+62+29+110+143 + MID 226+44+139 + ATT 195+180). Selling AMOAKO leaves that exact eleven intact - fielded ap stays 1395 - and banks 1.826.152. Selling WIDMER instead forces Amoako (ap 0) back into the eleven and drops fielded ap to 1366, i.e. it costs 29 points to raise 1.909.250. So Amoako is the only points-free sale on the books. SECOND REASON, VALUE: he is bleeding fast - mvt 2 falling, sdmvt -895.708 per day, tfhmvt -127.175 per two hours - and he has no points history at all, so the decline has no floor from performance. Georg bought him at +79,18% over mv (the third-highest premium in the whole measured log) and mvgl is -1.673.848; that loss is sunk and is NOT a reason to hold, since he optimises for points and Amoako produces none. AFTER THE SALE the squad is back to eleven (1/5/3/2), 5-3-2 only, zero bench - same fragility as now, no worse, because at eleven every player is fielded regardless of fitness. NOT URGENT relative to the buy: the buy has a 19:17Z deadline, this has until the 2026-09-04T18:30Z lock. Do it in that order and never the reverse.

buy.reason: Onyeka is the only buy, the bid is already in, and it should be left exactly where it is. Do not raise it, since it already clears the highest contested premium the log has ever measured, and do not withdraw it. The one genuinely new fact this run strengthens the case rather than weakening it: his profile records two goals and an assist from his two appearances, so the points behind his average are attacking returns rather than clean-sheet noise. The honest residual risk is unchanged, that a large premium rests on a single start at a promoted club, which is why the dated projected eleven is what makes this a calculated bid rather than a guess. Keitel is the fallback and only the fallback. He resolves tomorrow morning, after tonight's outcome is known, and he is worth a modest points gain if Onyeka is lost and worth precisely nothing if Onyeka lands, because his average does not displace any of the three midfielders in the shape that would then be legal. If he is ever taken, bid the high contested cluster and not the asking price; bidding at or near market value is how Nguefack was lost three separate times. Four arrivals were rejected: Moeller Wolfe, who has the best starter case of any of them but no points history at all and is a sixth defender; Suso, cheap but carrying a non-fit flag with no history; and El Aynaoui and Hwang, both simply beyond the uncommitted balance.
